source.title: Benzodiazepine and Z-Drug Use and the Risk of Developing Dementia

confidence_rationale: Large (>83 000 users vs >84 000 non-users), 13-year, population-registry cohort -- strong for an observational design and directly addressed to the Z-drug row that IMPL-026 previously had no evidence for at all. Held to 0.70 because the crude signal (HR 1.22) does not survive confounder adjustment, leaving only a dose-dependent residual, and because no sleep variable of any kind was measured.
failure_signatures: The crude association between benzodiazepine-receptor-agonist use and incident dementia (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.15-1.31) became non-significant after adjustment for confounders, so IMPL-026's unqualified 'Z-drugs: WORSENS' assignment is not supported at ordinary therapeutic exposure.
Elevated risk was confined to the highest dose stratum, implying a threshold or dose-dependent relation that IMPL-026's categorical WORSENS/NEUTRAL/IMPROVES schema cannot express.

The study measured no sleep architecture at all, so it cannot discriminate IMPL-026's proposed Phase 1/Phase 4 mechanism from any competing pathway (falls, sedation, anticholinergic co-prescription, reverse causation).

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a retrospective cohort of >83 000 benzodiazepine-receptor-agonist users and >84 000 non-users aged over 45 followed 2002-2015, the crude hazard ratio for incident dementia among users was 1.22 (95% CI 1.15-1.31) but lost significance after adjustment; increased risk persisted at the highest doses, and for shorter-acting benzodiazepines and Z-drugs, particularly in women.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the first literature entry bearing on IMPL-026's Z-drug row, which asserts 'WORSENS (less severe than classical BZDs but still harmful over years)'. The cohort supports the comparative half of that statement -- Z-drugs behave like a milder member of the same family, not like an architecture-preserving agent -- while withholding support from the 'harmful over years' half at standard doses.
mapping.mapping_caveat: IMPL-026 classifies medications by PREDICTED phase-specific pipeline disruption (INV-045 Phase 0-4). This paper measures neither phase-resolved consolidation nor any REE pipeline quantity; the mapping runs from a clinical endpoint back to a mechanism the study did not observe. Additionally, prescription-registry exposure is not adherence, and the female-predominant signal has no counterpart anywhere in IMPL-026's mechanism, which is specified without sex terms.
mapping.source_context: Catalan Health Service population registry; adults >45 years; 2002-2015; incident dementia endpoint.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality strong on size and follow-up, capped by the retrospective registry design. mapping_fidelity limited because the dementia endpoint is downstream of every pathway, not just the sleep-pipeline one. transfer_risk is the highest of this pull: confounding by indication plus a dose-response that could equally be confounding-by-severity.
